facts.text: Loring began as a Tlingit village called Kax̱.àan before Euro-Americans settled it in the 1870s as a fish camp.
In 1888 the Alaska Salmon Packing & Fur Company built a full cannery that could pack up to 1,800 cases of salmon daily.
The town’s peak population reached about 200 residents, most of whom were native Tlingit, with Chinese, Filipino, and Mexican workers living in bunkhouses.
A 1889 storm wrecked the steamship SS Ancon on a shoal in Naha Bay, leaving its boilers visible at low tide as a landmark.
By 1930 declining salmon runs and industry shifts forced the cannery to close, and the town was abandoned as buildings were dismantled.
Today, the only visible remnants are scattered ruins and the SS Ancon boilers, drawing curious explorers who hear the bay’s quiet wildlife.
